BYTE-LEVEL LEVER, and the one thing that decided this TU: the eight-byte state pair at +0x5004 must be spelled as a struct whose sole member is an ARRAY, struct Pair { int w[2]; }, not as two named scalars struct Pair { int a; int b; }. Seven members assign it (func_ov006_020ee2c4, 020ee3bc, 020ee3ec, 020ee44c, 020ee4e0, 020ee598, 020ee658) and with the two-scalar spelling all seven and only those seven came back DIFF at exactly 2 words: mwccarm scalarises the copy member-by-member and emits ldr/str/ldr/str, where the cartridge hoists both loads -- ldr r2,[r1]; ldr r1,[r1,#4]; str r2,[r0,#4]; str r1,[r0,#8]. The array member makes the compiler copy the object as a unit and reproduces the ROM's schedule; changing that one declaration took the TU from 10/17 to 17/17. The already-promoted twin src/minigames/d_s_mg_jump2.cpp uses the same array spelling for the same +0x5004 construct and matches 29/29, so this is the ov006 house form and not a one-off. The legacy shards disagreed among themselves -- 020ee3bc, 020ee4e0 and 020ee598 used the two-scalar form, 020ee3ec, 020ee44c and 020ee658 the array form -- and each was a separate compilation unit, so each matched alone; unifying them is what exposed the difference. Merging shards can surface a lever that no shard could see.

PRAGMA MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The legacy shard src/func_ov006_020ee5b8.c carried #pragma optimize_for_size on. It was dropped rather than bracketed, and func_ov006_020ee5b8 still MATCHes, so the pragma is not load-bearing for this range and no push/pop bracket is needed -- the same result dScMgRoulette_c measured. This TU sets no pragmas at all.
